newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM to start flight bookings via Internet.
newsitem.headline: KLM to start flight bookings via Internet.

text.p: KLM passengers will soon be able to book their flights through Internet, the worldwide network of computers linked via telephone lines, the Dutch national carrier said on Monday.
"KLM will be launching a worldwide timetable for all its flights and those of its partners before the end of the year," spokesman Hugo Baas said.
Initially the service would be limited to companies and participants in KLM's customer loyalty programme, Baas said, adding full introduction of Internet reservations would depend on consumer demand.
Users will be able to call up flight information and book seats through the reservations site, but payments will not be made on-line for security reasons.
Bookings will initially be limited to outbound flights from the Netherlands.
KLM already offers Dutch Internet users a 'click and go' option for selected flights, but this is subject to confirmation of the reservation by telephone.
